items.title: 1.6 Assessment of total uncertainty in the final result

source_refs.note: Topic 1.6 with Examples 1.1 to 1.3, the Thumb Rule for Total Uncertainty box and the colour-printing and light-travel side boxes (PDF 12-14, printed 9-11).

blocks.text: Knowing the uncertainties in all the factors involved in a calculation, the maximum possible uncertainty or error in the final result can be found as follows:
Absolute uncertainties are added. For example, the distance between two positions x₁ = 15.4 ± 0.1 cm and x₂ = 25.6 cm ± 0.1 cm is recorded as:
and addition of two lengths is: ℓ₁ = 8.5 ± 0.1 cm and ℓ₂ = 12.6 ± 0.1 cm recorded as:
Colour printing uses just four colours-cyan, magenta, yellow and black to produce the entire range of colours. All the colours in this book have been made from just these four colours.
blocks.title: For your information

blocks.text: Percentage uncertainties are added. For example, the maximum possible uncertainty in the value of resistance R of a conductor determined by the potential difference V applied across the conductor resulting in current flowing through it is estimated as under:

blocks.text_alt: Percentage uncertainty in V = (0.1 V / 3.4 V) × 100 = 3%
Percentage uncertainty in I = (0.05 A / 0.68 A) × 100 = 7%

blocks.text: For addition and subtraction: Absolute uncertainties are added. For multiplication and division: Percentage uncertainties are added. For power factor: Power factor × Percentage uncertainty.
blocks.title: Thumb Rule for Total Uncertainty

blocks.text: Hence, total percentage uncertainty in the value of R is 3 + 7 = 10%
The value of R will be written as:
Hence, R = 5.0 ± 0.5 ohms, uncertainty being an estimate only, is recorded by one significant figure.

blocks.caption: Travel time of light (For your information)

blocks.text: The travel time of light from the Moon to the Earth is printed as 1 min 20 s. The Moon is about 3.84 × 10⁸ m away, so light takes about 1.3 s (1.28 s).
blocks.title: Book correction

blocks.text: The percentage uncertainty is multiplied by the power factor in the formula. For example, the calculation of cross-sectional area of a cylinder of radius r = 1.25 cm using formula for Area A = πr² is given by the %age uncertainty which is A = 2 × %age uncertainty in radius r. As uncertainty is multiplied by power factor, it increases the precision demand of measurement. When the radius of a small sphere is measured as 1.25 cm by Vernier Callipers with least count 0.01 cm, then

blocks.latex: \text{The radius } r \text{ is recorded as}\quad r = 1.25 \pm 0.01\ \text{cm}
blocks.text_alt: The radius r is recorded as r = 1.25 ± 0.01 cm

blocks.latex: \%\text{age uncertainty in radius } r \text{ is}\quad r = \frac{0.01}{1.25} \times 100 = 0.8\%
blocks.text_alt: %age uncertainty in radius r is r = (0.01 / 1.25) × 100 = 0.8%
Total percentage uncertainty in area A = 2 × 0.8 = 1.6%

blocks.text: Thus, the result should be recorded as A = 4.91 ± 0.08 cm
The unit of area is printed as cm. Area is measured in square centimetres: A = 4.91 ± 0.08 cm².
blocks.title: Book correction
Example 1.1
blocks.problem: The length, breadth and thickness of a metal sheet are 2.03 m, 1.22 m and 0.95 cm respectively. Calculate the volume of the sheet correct up to the appropriate significant digits.
steps: As the factor 0.95 cm has minimum number of significant figures equal to two, therefore, volume is recorded up to 2 significant figures, hence,

blocks.title: Example 1.2
blocks.problem: The mass of a metal box measured by a lever balance is 3.25 kg. Two silver coins of masses 10.01 g and 10.02 g measured by a beam balance are added to it. What is now the total mass of the box correct up to the appropriate precision?
steps: Total mass when silver coins are added to box = 3.25 kg + 0.01001 kg + 0.01002 kg = 3.27003 kg
Since least precise mass is 3.25 kg, having two decimal places, hence, total mass should be reported to 2 decimal places which is the appropriate precision.

blocks.title: Example 1.3
blocks.problem: The diameter and length of a metal cylinder measured with the help of Vernier Callipers of least count 0.01 cm are 1.25 cm and 3.35 cm, respectively. Calculate the volume V of the cylinder and uncertainty in it.
steps: Given: Diameter d = 1.25 cm with least count 0.01 cm
Length ℓ = 3.35 cm with least count 0.01 cm
Total uncertainty in V = 2 (%age uncertainty in diameter) + (%age uncertainty in length) = 2 × 0.8 + 0.3 = 1.9 %
Then V = 3.14 × (1.25 cm)² × 3.35 cm/4 = 4.1089842 cm³ with 1.9 % uncertainty
blocks.answer: Thus V = (4.11 ± 0.08) cm³, where 4.11 cm³ is calculated volume and 0.08 is the uncertainty in it.
